quotes.why: Tsongkhapa's own opening, which p3 reproduces almost word for word — the frame within which the first preliminary is set.
The gser phreng's continuation: the chief commentaries are 'the four great trail-blazers, as earlier masters call them' — the position p6 will refuse.
The root verse that names both terms the four preliminaries stand between — the Prajñāpāramitā and the eight subjects. Found by direct search.
Haribhadra takes p3's sūtra citation as the brief statement (མདོར་བསྟན) of complete enlightenment, and reads it with བརྩོན་པར་བྱའོ where p3 has བསླབ་པར་བྱའོ.
Dharmamitra labels the same lemma as belonging to the middling Mother, which fixes which sūtra p3 is quoting.
Vasubandhu reads the same lemma as the brief statement of the bodhisattva's intention, before the extensive exposition — a third witness to its structural role.
A second Tibetan spyi don quotes the lemma with a third reading, འདོད་པས … བསླབ་པར་བྱའོ, and to the same purpose.
Haribhadra glosses the sūtra's 'perfection of wisdom' as sarvākārajñatā — the Ornament's frame already applied to the sūtra's words.
The same phrase glossed as mārgajñatā in a different context, showing the gloss is positional rather than lexical.
Haribhadra's taxonomy of small, middling and great entrustment, which places p3's second citation precisely.
Jamyang Zhepa's Gomang introduction opens with the same three-stage career and fills in every particular p3 leaves blank.
The Gomang text supplies the Abhidharmakośa proof for the three countless aeons that p3 asserts without support.
